text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: streaming p99 spike (SSE/WebSocket) for hosted-api routes /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. p99=12.8s, p95=1.2s, streaming stalls 3.2%. First anomalous rollout signal ~15:20 UTC.

alex: ack, I'm oncall. Triage starting. Which regions/populations?

maya: seeing concentrated impact in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Envoy proxies showing long buffer flush times and increased 504s. Runtime logs show lots of 'write EPIPE' and retry storms from clients.

alex: summary from dashboards: jump in active concurrent streams x3 after yesterday's deploy, per-worker queue depth spiked. p95 still okay, p99 terrible. Could be client backpressure + proxy buffering.

jon: CS: acme-inc and several staging customers reporting stalled streams then reconnects (ticket #4567). Impacted sessions are mostly long-running chat sessions. Estimated affected requests ~0.5% but several high-value tenants.

alex: mitigation plan (short):
1) route a small % of streaming traffic to non-streaming fallback (polling) for affected tenants
2) disable response buffering in proxy for SSE endpoints, bump write_timeout
3) scale runtime streaming pool and reduce per-worker max concurrent streams
4) temporarily rate-limit high-churn clients/IPs

rachel: I can push proxy config to disable response buffering and increase write_timeout to 15s in us-west-2 canary. Will run canary first.

maya: I'll cycle streaming workers: reduce max_concurrency from 16 -> 8 and restart rolling. Also enable more aggressive KV/prefix cache for recurrent prompts to cut token generation time.

alex: cutting 10% of prod streaming traffic to fallback for acme-inc (to reduce surface area) with redwoodctl. Command: 
```
# cut traffic to fallback for canary
redwoodctl traffic split --route /v1/stream --from=prod --to=fallback --percent=10 --region=us-west-2\```

oncall-bot: deploy started by rachel at 15:28 UTC. CI green. Rolling canary to us-west-2.

rachel: canary applied in us-west-2. Watching metrics (p99, proxy write latency, connection resets).

maya: restarted first runtime node in us-west-2. Host-level 'write EPIPE' count dropped ~80% on that host. p99 us-west-2 reduced from 12.8s -> 4.5s. Improvement but not at SLO yet.

alex: good. Continue rolling rest. Also enable prefix/KV cache for chat sessions where applicable to reduce repeated decoding time.

jon: CS update sent to acme-inc: "we've enabled fallback for a subset of your streams and are rolling mitigations; some sessions may see polling behavior briefly." Posted at 15:35 UTC.

alex: @infra-team please check for network flapping. Connection resets look correlated to client side closes but want confirmation there's no LB or network error.

infra-team: investigating. No packet loss on fabric. Resets align with client timeouts and heavy buffer pressure at proxy (Envoy).

rachel: canary in eu-west-1 applied. p99 in eu-west-1 down to 3.9s. Global p99 trending down after successive rollouts and worker restarts.

oncall-bot: SLO WATCH: p99>2s for 10+ minutes. Paging policy triggered; pagerduty notified.

alex: paging SRE lead and runtime lead. Additional mitigations: reduce default chunk size to 2KB, enable earlier force-flush in runtime codepath, and bump autoscale target by +20% for streaming pool.

maya: applied chunk size tweak on two streaming pods and restarted. Client-side backpressure metrics show fewer retries and smaller write latency variance. Proxy 504 count decreasing.

alex: current status: p99 ~2.1s global, us-west-2 ~2.0s, eu-west-1 ~2.3s. Still fragile. Will continue monitoring and hold rollout of the yesterday change until RCA.

jon: handoff note for night oncall: acme-inc on fallback (10% traffic), mitigations applied (proxy buffering disabled, chunk size lowered, workers cycled, autoscale bumped). Primary risk: if active stream count spikes again, p99 will regress. CS ticket #4567 pinned.

rachel: ack taking handoff. Will monitor for 2 hours, escalate if p99 > 2.5s or error rate increases.

oncall-bot: Incident ID INC-20241004-27. Status: mitigation in progress, monitoring. Thread will be updated with any new changes. :white_check_mark:
